title: improv·artist · obsessive (Yayoi Kusama)
mutation_directive: improv artist: obsessive via Yayoi Kusama

improv_extras.practice: infinite polka-dot repetition; pumpkins; mirror-room infinity; scale and pattern as obsession made visible

v1.feedback: The 3×3 grid of Lucy statues is a literal interpretation of Kusama's repetition but misses the obsessive, overwhelming quality — nine copies in a neat grid reads as a layout exercise, not infinity made visible. The polka-dot concept only shows up as round point sprites, not as actual dots patterning the surface; true Kusama would have spherical dots growing on or erupting from the mesh skin. The red/white/yellow palette is on-theme but the additive blending washes it into hot pink noise at overlap zones, losing the crisp dot-on-field contrast that defines her work. A stronger version would tile dozens of smaller Lucys in a logarithmic spiral or mirror-room recursion, apply actual surface-mapped polka dots via a dot-product threshold in the fragment shader, and use a restrained red-on-white or yellow-on-black field rather than additive glow.

v2.feedback: The Kusama polka-dot concept lands clearly — red dots on ivory Lucy with concentric repetition and a dotted floor sell the infinity-room obsession. The central figure is well-framed and readable, and the ring layout gives genuine depth. To push it further: the outer ring copies are too small and sparse to read as anything but noise at distance — either increase their particle count or fade them into a fog/mirror boundary. The breathing pulse is nearly invisible; lean into the obsessive repetition more by having dot frequency or size oscillate per-copy with slight phase offsets, so the field feels alive rather than static. A subtle reflection or mirrored duplicate below the floor plane would strengthen the infinity-room reference considerably.
